subject.title: Crons ejecutaron mensajes de WhatsApp a la 1 AM fuera de horario y no se podían detener

question: Should this issue be solved by landing only the restart catch-up schedule boundary, or should OpenClaw also add a first-class emergency halt/delete-cancels-active-sends flow for cron outbound delivery?
rationale: Current main still has the replay behavior, but the already-open conflicting PR covers only the schedule-activation subset while the stop/delete/emergency behavior changes operator UX and cancellation semantics.

options.title: Land replay boundary first
options.body: Review, rebase, or replace the schedule-activation fix from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92398, then track emergency halt semantics as follow-up work.

options.title: Scope one broader cron safety PR
options.body: Require a single design that combines schedule-bounded replay with active-run cancellation and user-facing halt behavior before implementation proceeds.

options.title: Defer emergency halt
options.body: Fix only the unsafe restart replay and explicitly leave gateway-wide outbound stop behavior out of scope for now.

recommendation.title: Land replay boundary first
recommendation.body: Review, rebase, or replace the schedule-activation fix from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92398, then track emergency halt semantics as follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history on the cron startup catch-up code and related scheduler refactors.
